source.title: Logit Distance Bounds Representational Similarity
source.citation: Beatrix M. G. Nielsen et al., 2026
source.authors: Beatrix M. G. Nielsen; E. Marconato; Luigi Gresele; Andrea Dittadi; Simon Buchholz

record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures teacher–student representational alignment after training with different distillation objectives. It uses mCCA and a new linear-identifiability dissimilarity rather than testing convergence with scale or across modalities.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own experimental results on representational similarity are included below. Theoretical examples in Appendices G and H are included as stated constructed-model measurements. Results cited from other studies, classification accuracy, and distribution-distance values that do not measure representational alignment are not rows. The experiments do not test natural convergence across model scales, independent training seeds, or modalities.
record.test_reason: All empirical rows compare distilled students with the teacher they were explicitly trained to match. The alignment is induced by the training objective, not arising between independently trained models. The study does not measure natural convergence across scale, seeds, architectures or modalities, so it tests no version. Its theory is that small logit distance implies linear similarity and small KL does not. That is an identifiability argument about distributionally close models. It only touches V4 and V7 in discussion; the paper notes Huh et al.'s limited convergence under linear metrics and cites other possible drivers.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. Also: they prove logit distance is a metric that upper-bounds their drep dissimilarity and lower-bounds mCCA. KL bounds logit distance only under a probability lower bound, and the bound is weak in practice. Minimizing logit distance yields students more linearly similar to their teachers than KL distillation. Extension to LLM distillation is future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes logit-distance bounds and compares KL-based, L1-logit, and squared-logit distillation; it does not reproduce the original sources’ convergence measurements or scale sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Representational similarity differs by distillation objective. On CIFAR, L1 and L2 have similar mCCA but different drep. The SUB ablation reports different mCCA trends by objective as student representation dimension varies.

fits_no_version.finding: Students distilled with KL match teacher accuracy but have much lower linear similarity to the teacher than logit-distance students. KL mCCA is 0.58/0.515/0.42 vs about 0.99/0.77/0.99 for L1 and L2 students (Synth/CIFAR/SUB).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which distillation objective preserves a teacher's linear representational structure (KL vs logit distance).

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed model pairs show mCCA can be 1 on embeddings, or on both embeddings and unembeddings, while unembeddings or output distributions differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-representation mCCA is insufficient to establish model equivalence (similarity-metric adequacy).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The experiments are limited to Synth, CIFAR 100, and SUB distillation, not large language models or cross-modal model pairs. The authors note assumptions about label count and general position, and that experiments on larger models remain future work. For CIFAR and SUB, drep uses randomly sampled label subsets rather than all possible subsets; the dimension-ablation figure gives no exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Classification accuracy and dKL/dlogit values in Tables 1–4 and Appendix L.5 were not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure representational alignment. Figure 8 accuracy measures were also left out; the similarity-relevant figure results are recorded in r19–r21.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no independently trained heterogeneous models.
No cross-modal comparison; the authors say it is out of scope.
No comparison across independently initialized seeds of the same architecture.
No mapping between independently trained models. Teacher–student linear similarity is induced by distillation.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
No measurement of convergence across metrics, neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs for naturally trained model pairs.
No measurement of the extent of natural convergence or its causes. Only distillation-objective effects on induced alignment.

record.verdict_notes: I override the reader's 'tests/T2' and its V4, V6 and V7 labels. All alignment here is between a student and the teacher it was trained to imitate, which the rules treat as induced, not a test of convergence. The discussion mentions Huh et al.'s limited linear convergence and suggests early training dynamics may drive similarity under cross-entropy. These are remarks, not results.

versions.untested_parts: No model-scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities to test convergence as size and capability increase.
No paired image–caption or other cross-modal representation comparison.
Student seeds are aggregated for teacher–student comparisons; the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across independently initialized models of the same architecture.
Tests teacher–student alignment in distillation settings using mCCA and drep; does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or mappings across arbitrary model pairs.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
Compares mCCA and drep and reports dataset/objective-dependent results, but does not test neighbour-count settings, out-of-distribution inputs, or a broad set of alternative similarity measures.
Tests how distillation objective relates to teacher–student alignment. Does not isolate shared training data, test a common model of reality, or measure a convergence plateau.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: L1- and L2-distilled students on Synth and SUB
reader_labels.reason: Their reported drep and mCCA show strong teacher–student alignment, including mCCA 0.999 on Synth and 0.99 on SUB (r3–r6, r15–r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR students and KL-distilled students across the tested datasets
reader_labels.reason: CIFAR mCCA is 0.763–0.767 rather than near 1, and KL-student similarity is much weaker than logit-distance student similarity (r1–r2, r7–r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR L1- versus L2-distilled students; constructed examples in Appendices G and H
reader_labels.reason: On CIFAR, mCCA is nearly the same for L1 and L2 while drep differs; the constructed examples also show that high mCCA for an individual representation set need not establish joint representational or distributional equivalence (r9–r12, r22–r25).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Teacher–student distillation objectives on Synth, CIFAR 100, and SUB
reader_labels.reason: Alignment depends strongly on the distillation objective: KL students fare substantially worse than L1/L2 students, while CIFAR alignment remains incomplete even for the latter (r1–r18).
